classification.difficultyReason: Apply squared and cubed scale factors in reverse and convert square and cubic units.

content.prompt: As part of a major development, an architect designed a building and had a model made to a scale of $1:400$; that is, $1\text{ cm}$ on the model is $4\text{ m}$ on the building.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The external surface area of the building is $10\,600\text{ m}^2$. Calculate the external surface area of the model, in $\text{cm}^2$.

answer.worked:
The model's lengths are $\frac{1}{400}$ of the building's lengths, so its surface area is multiplied by $\left(\frac{1}{400}\right)^2$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{model}}&=10\,600\times\left(\frac{1}{400}\right)^2\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{model}}&=0.06625\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{model}}&=0.06625\times100^2\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{model}}&=662.5\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The volume of the building is $60\,000\text{ m}^3$. Calculate the volume of the model, in $\text{cm}^3$.

answer.worked:
The model's volume is multiplied by $\left(\frac{1}{400}\right)^3$.
$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{model}}&=60\,000\times\left(\frac{1}{400}\right)^3\text{ m}^3\\V_{\text{model}}&=0.0009375\text{ m}^3\\V_{\text{model}}&=0.0009375\times100^3\text{ cm}^3\\V_{\text{model}}&=937.5\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$
